question.stem:
A company needs to use Amazon Aurora as the Amazon RDS database engine for its web application. The Solutions Architect has been instructed to implement a 90-day RDS backup retention policy.
Which of the following options can satisfy the given requirement?
options: Create an AWS Backup plan to take daily snapshots with a retention period of 90 days.
Configure RDS to export the automated snapshot automatically to Amazon S3 and create a lifecycle policy to delete the object after 90 days.
Configure an automated backup and set the backup retention period to 90 days.
Create a daily scheduled event using Amazon EventBridge and AWS Lambda to directly download the RDS automated snapshot to an Amazon S3 bucket. Archive snapshots older than 90 days to Glacier.
question.explanation: RDS/Aurora automated backups keep a maximum of 35 days, so a 90-day retention needs AWS Backup: a backup plan with a daily rule and 90-day retention (fully managed, no code). Setting the automated backup retention to 90 days is not possible. Exporting snapshots to S3 is a manual/scripted export to Parquet that is not an automatic feature of automated backups and is not directly restorable. You cannot directly download RDS snapshots to S3 with a Lambda function.

concept: RDS/Aurora backups: automated backups max 35 days, use AWS Backup for longer retention
tests: Knowing the automated backup retention limit for RDS/Aurora (35 days) and that longer retention (e.g. 90 days) is done with AWS Backup plans (or manual snapshots).
expected: An AWS Backup plan with a daily backup rule and a 90-day retention. Triggers: 'Aurora', '90-day backup retention', RDS automated backups top out at 35 days.
why_not: Automated backup retention can't exceed 35 days, so option 3 can't be configured. S3 export is not an automatic feature of automated snapshots, produces Parquet files and is not a restorable backup. A Lambda can't just download an RDS snapshot to S3, and building this yourself is high overhead.
